title: single-object Kadam material carrying inline data-URI icon and hero image

source.name: Kadam Feed and RTB contracts, including in-page and clickunder examples
source.notes: All source records are retained in assets/sources.json by reference.sourceIds.

modifications: All ids, domains, prices, timestamps, creative text and URLs independently authored.

icon_url and image_url carry a tiny inline data: URI PNG instead of a hosted file, so the sealed preview frame's img-src data: blob: policy can load them without the explicit fetch action — this proves the full-render path for the documented Kadam field set, which the sibling push-kadam-icon-notice case (https assets, partial render) does not exercise.

No OpenRTB or GET-URL request is invented for this response-only scenario: the Kadam feed request query string has no registered decoder (push-kadam-icon-notice, known gap DEF-107), so this case exercises the response side alone instead of repeating that already-recorded gap.
provenance.sanitized: No real visitor or subscriber data. click_url/nurl use reserved .test hostnames and are not intended to be fetched; icon_url/image_url are self-contained data: URIs with no external network access at all.

pairApplicability.note: Response-only: the Kadam feed's documented GET request query string has no registered decoder (DEF-107), so only the documented single-object response material shape is exercised here.

response.title: A tidy garden shed
response.text: Repaint the shed before the rain arrives.

specNotes: Kadam documents the material contract as title/text/image_url/icon_url/click_url/cpc/nurl on a single object as well as inside an array (formats-feeds map §1.1/§1.2); push-kadam-icon-notice already covers the array form, so this case is the single-object counterpart.

icon_url and image_url are inline data: URIs so the sealed preview frame's img-src data: blob: policy renders both assets immediately, without the explicit "Load images" action — proving the full-render path, not only the always-blocked https path the sibling Kadam case already covers.

Desired capability: detectFeedFormat recognizes a cleanly-validated, documented push material as push regardless of whether its image/icon keys carry the `_url` suffix. Existing product acceptance is not the validity oracle.
The documented vendor ad type must be identified in the merged format result. Public Core vocabulary uses pops for pop traffic; this is a vendor capability expectation, not an invented IAB extension.
notes: Core observations in the source archive were deliberately excluded from expectations. Protocol metadata may describe a vendor-specific 2.x carrier; it does not claim a normative minor-version inference.
